prompt: What is the difference between a view and a materialised view in BigQuery?

choices.text: Only the materialised view stores a result
choices.why: Right. That stored result is what saves the reading.

choices.text: A materialised view is a view in another project
choices.why: Projects have nothing to do with it.

choices.text: A view is cached for a day; a materialised view forever
choices.why: A view stores nothing, and a materialised view is refreshed.

choices.text: Only a materialised view can be queried with SQL
choices.why: Both are queried with SQL.

prompt: Why can `SUM(total_cents)` be maintained incrementally and a median cannot?
hint: Combine an old result with the new rows.

choices.text: Sums add up; medians do not
choices.why: Right. That is the restriction's reason.

choices.text: Medians are not in GoogleSQL
choices.why: GoogleSQL computes quantiles; they just cannot be combined.

choices.text: Sums are smaller to store
choices.why: Size is not what decides it.

choices.text: A median needs the time of day
choices.why: Time-dependent functions are a separate restriction.

prompt: New orders arrived ten minutes ago and the view has not been refreshed yet. What does a query on the view return, without `max_staleness`?

choices.text: The stored result, ten minutes old
choices.why: Only `max_staleness` allows a stale answer.

choices.text: An error until the refresh
choices.why: The view is always queryable.

choices.text: Stored rows plus the new ones
choices.why: Right. The delta is read from the base table.

choices.text: The base table, scanned in full
choices.why: Only the rows since the refresh are read from it.

prompt: Quitanda rewrites the whole `orders` table every night. What does that do to a materialised view over it?

choices.text: Nothing: views ignore rewrites of the base
choices.why: A rewrite changes every row the view aggregated.

choices.text: It makes the view free to refresh
choices.why: A full recomputation is the dearest refresh.

choices.text: It recomputes everything, every time
choices.why: Right. Changed rows, not new rows.

choices.text: The view is deleted
choices.why: It is invalidated and recomputed, not deleted.

prompt: The third run of `incremental.py` read 16,359 order rows to add one day. The first read 1,228,759 for 59 days. What fraction of the first did the third read? Give three decimal places.
What did the second run of `incremental.py`, with nothing new, read?
hint: It looks for days it has not seen.

choices.text: The whole table, to check it
choices.why: It compared folder names and read no orders.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. A refresh with no change costs nothing.

choices.text: The last day again
choices.why: The last day was already aggregated.

choices.text: Only the footers
choices.why: It opened no Parquet file at all.

prompt: The check returned zero differences. What does that establish?
hint: `EXCEPT` keeps rows of the first query missing from the second.

choices.text: That DuckDB and BigQuery agree
choices.why: BigQuery never ran.

choices.text: Incremental equals full
choices.why: Right. The bookkeeping lost nothing.

choices.text: That the aggregate is smaller than the table
choices.why: True, but not what `EXCEPT` measured.

choices.text: That no order was corrected
choices.why: It compares results, not history.

prompt: Why should a materialised view be partitioned like its base table, by the lesson's argument?
hint: Think of a correction to one day.

choices.text: So that BigQuery can read both with one slot
choices.why: Slots have nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Because a view must copy its base table's options
choices.why: It may differ; it is a choice.

choices.text: So a correction to one day costs recomputing one day
choices.why: Right. The partition is the unit of recomputation.

choices.text: To get long-term storage pricing
choices.why: That follows writes, not the alignment.

prompt: What does smart tuning do?

choices.text: Points base-table queries at a view
choices.why: Right. The dashboard still says `FROM orders`.

choices.text: Tunes the number of slots a reservation holds
choices.why: That is the autoscaler of lesson 14.

choices.text: Picks the clustering columns
choices.why: Clustering is chosen by whoever creates the table.

choices.text: Compresses the view
choices.why: Compression is the storage's, invisible.

prompt: The view holds `dt`, `district`, `orders` and `sales`. Which query cannot be rewritten to read it?
hint: An aggregate cannot be taken apart.

choices.text: Sales per district for September
choices.why: Everything it needs is in the view.

choices.text: Orders per day
choices.why: A sum of the view's `orders` per `dt`.

choices.text: Sales per store
choices.why: Right. The view has no `store_id`.

choices.text: Total sales of 29 September
choices.why: A sum of the view's eight rows for that day.

prompt: `bqbill.py` printed 31,457,280 bytes billed for the base table and 10,485,760 for the view. How many times the view's bill is the base table's?
A dashboard adds a column the view does not have. What happens to its queries?

choices.text: They fail with an error naming the view
choices.why: Nothing fails; the rewrite just does not happen.

choices.text: They read the base table, silently
choices.why: Right. Read what the job actually did.

choices.text: BigQuery adds the column to the view
choices.why: A view's definition never changes by itself.

choices.text: They are served from the cache
choices.why: The cache needs the same query on unchanged tables.

prompt: What runs a scheduled query on its timetable?
hint: The same one that loads Google Ads data on a schedule.

choices.text: Cloud Scheduler
choices.why: A separate product; scheduled queries do not need it.

choices.text: The BigQuery Data Transfer Service
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: BI Engine
choices.why: BI Engine is memory, not a scheduler.

choices.text: Cloud Composer
choices.why: Composer is lesson 24's, for chains of steps.

prompt: Why does the scheduled query use `MERGE` rather than `INSERT`?

choices.text: `INSERT` is not allowed in a scheduled query
choices.why: It is allowed; it is just unsafe to repeat.

choices.text: Repeating a run must not add the day twice
choices.why: Right. Safe to repeat.

choices.text: `MERGE` reads fewer bytes
choices.why: Both read the same source rows.

choices.text: Medians need `MERGE`
choices.why: The median is computed by the `SELECT` inside.

prompt: Besides `@run_date`, the service fills a second parameter with the instant the run was scheduled for, `@run___`.
hint: An underscore, then a word of four letters.

prompt: A scheduled query fails one night and nobody set a notification. What does the dashboard show the next morning?
hint: Where does a failed run show?

choices.text: An error banner
choices.why: Nothing tells the dashboard the run failed.

choices.text: The previous results, as if current
choices.why: Right. Only the run history, or a notification, says otherwise.

choices.text: Nothing, since the table is emptied
choices.why: A failed run writes nothing, so the old rows stay.

choices.text: Yesterday's base table
choices.why: The dashboard reads the destination table.

prompt: A BI Engine reservation of 5 GiB in southamerica-east1 is kept for a month. By the page's monthly price, what does it cost, in USD?
On demand, what does a BI Engine-accelerated query pay for the stage that reads the table?

choices.text: Half the bytes
choices.why: There is no half price.

choices.text: Nothing: 0 scanned bytes
choices.why: Right. The memory is paid for instead.

choices.text: The 10 MB minimum
choices.why: The page says 0 scanned bytes for that stage.

choices.text: The same as without it
choices.why: Then it would only buy speed; it buys the bytes too.

prompt: Lesson 15's partitioned dashboard cost 2.90 USD a month at a thousand times Quitanda's size. Is 2 GiB of BI Engine worth buying for it?

choices.text: Yes, since accelerated reads are free
choices.why: The memory costs 109.35 a month to save 2.90.

choices.text: No: 109.35 USD of memory to save 2.90
choices.why: Right. Make the answer small first.

choices.text: Yes, if it is on a 3-year commitment
choices.why: BI Engine has no such commitment of its own.

choices.text: No, since BI Engine only works on Standard edition
choices.why: The page offers it with on demand and editions alike.

prompt: Put the steps of this lesson's advice for a slow, expensive dashboard in order.
items: Partition and cluster the base table
Keep the answer in a materialised view, or a scheduled query
Check from the job statistics that the dashboard reads it
Put BI Engine in front of the small tables, if they still read enough to matter

prompt: Match each tool to the job it does.
hint: One right-hand option belongs to a lesson before this one.

pairs.right: Keeps an incremental aggregate current, maintained by BigQuery
Runs any SQL on a timetable and writes its result
Sends a base-table query to a view that can answer it
Serves the reading stage from memory, billed by the GiB-hour

right_distractors: Refuses a query that would bill too much
